Fiftieth
fif'-tī-eth
adj. (the ordinal of fifty — in the law, the year of jubile)
From fifty, Saxon fiftig. Its two great occurrences are in one law: after seven sabbaths of years, forty and nine years, the fiftieth year is hallowed and liberty is proclaimed.

Biblical Definition

“And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family” (Lev 25:10). Every fiftieth year: debts released, Hebrew servants freed, land returned to the family that had lost it. Two returns are commanded — to a possession and to a family — and the second is not decoration; the law is as concerned with households reconstituted as with acres restored. “A jubile shall that fiftieth year be unto you: ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of itself in it, nor gather the grapes in it of thy vine undressed” (Lev 25:11) — following the forty-ninth, which was itself a sabbath year, so that Israel was asked to trust God for two harvests they had not planted. The kings' chronicles use the ordinal in the ordinary way to date reigns: Pekahiah began to reign “in the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah” (2Ki 15:23). Our Lord opened His ministry by reading Isaiah 61 in the synagogue at Nazareth — to preach deliverance to the captives… to preach the acceptable year of the LORD — and sat down and said, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears. The jubilee trumpet was a shadow; He is the liberty.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) gives fiftieth as the ordinal of fifty; and jubilee as, among the Israelites, every fiftieth year, being the year following the revolution of seven weeks of years, at which time all slaves were liberated and lands returned to their former owners.

FIFTIETH, a. The ordinal of fifty; as the fiftieth part of a foot.

JUBILEE, n. Among the Israelites, every fiftieth year, being the year following the revolution of seven weeks of years, at which time all the slaves were liberated, and all lands which had been alienated during the whole period reverted to their former owners.

1. A season of great public joy and festivity.

LIBERTY, n. Freedom from restraint; the power of acting as one thinks fit.

Key Scripture

Lev 25:10 — "And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family."

Lev 25:11 — "A jubile shall that fiftieth year be unto you: ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of itself in it, nor gather the grapes in it of thy vine undressed."

2Ki 15:23 — "In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two years."

Modern Corruption

The jubilee is enlisted as a programme of economic redistribution; Leviticus makes it the restoration of families to their own inheritance under a divine title.

expand to see more

Leviticus 25 is regularly conscripted for modern redistributive politics, and the fit is poor in both directions. The jubilee does not abolish property; it protects it, by returning each family to its own inheritance and preventing the permanent accumulation of land in a few hands. Nothing is transferred to the state, no central authority administers it, and the restoration is to a household rather than to a class. Equally, the chapter refuses the absolutist reading of ownership: the land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. Human title is real and derived, and the jubilee is the yearly reminder of whose it is.

What must not be lost in the argument is the gospel shape of the year. Debt cancelled, bondmen freed, the exile restored to his family, and a trumpet on the day of atonement to start it — liberty proclaimed on the very day the blood was carried into the holiest. Our Lord read the jubilee text at Nazareth and applied it to Himself. The believer's release from a debt he could never repay, and his restoration to a family and an inheritance, is the substance of which the fiftieth year was the shadow.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yobel (H3104), the jubile — a ram's horn, and the year it announced; deror (H1865), liberty, release; 'achuzzah (H272), a possession.

expand to see more

Hebrew yobel (H3104) — a ram's horn, and by extension the year proclaimed by it; Leviticus 25:10-13.

Hebrew deror (H1865) — liberty, a free running; Leviticus 25:10, Isaiah 61:1, Jeremiah 34:8 — the word inscribed on the Liberty Bell.

Hebrew 'achuzzah (H272) — a possession, a holding; what every man returned to.

Hebrew mishpachah (H4940) — a family, a clan; the second return the law commands.

Greek eniauton kuriou dekton — the acceptable year of the Lord; Luke 4:19, read by our Lord at Nazareth.

Usage

"“Ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty”."

"“Return every man unto his possession… every man unto his family” — two returns."

"“Ye shall not sow, neither reap” — the second unplanted year in a row."
